items.title: Retirement: Azure VMware Solution License-included service will be retired August 30, 2027
items.description:
In November last year Broadcom changed its VMware licensing policies across all hyperscaler platforms to require customers to “bring your own” portable license for VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF).

What’s changing?

On August 30, 2027, as a result of the latest Broadcom VCF licensing change, the AVS license-included service will be retired.  Customers currently using license-included Reserved Instance (RI) SKUs will be required to purchase portable Broadcom VCF Licenses and transition to an AVS VCF BYOL SKU or exit AVS prior to August 30, 2027, to avoid service disruption on August 31, 2027.

Take Action Today:

Allow plenty of time to purchase VCF licenses from Broadcom and complete the transition to AVS VCF BYOL. For customers evaluating modernization opportunities, start assessing current AVS environments immediately, and develop a transition roadmap to ensure you have ample time to exit AVS and avoid service disruption on August 31, 2027.

Contact your account team to plan your transition.

Key Dates and Transition Details
  • August 30, 2027 Last Day of all AVS license-included services
  • AVS License-included RIs Microsoft allows for the exchange of Reservations with expiration dates beyond August 30, 2027
  • AVS License-included PayGo SKUs will retire on October 15, 2026
  • UPDATE AV36 SKU Retirement is now August 30, 2027
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Managed Instance on Azure App Service
items.description:
Managed Instance on Azure App Service is now generally available. 

Managed Instance helps organizations migrate web applications to Azure App Service with minimal configuration and no code changes. Applications running on-premises or in virtual machines can move to a fully managed PaaS environment while maintaining compatibility with Windows-specific dependencies.

Many business-critical .NET applications rely on Windows services, third-party libraries, custom runtimes, and other components that can make modernization challenging. Managed Instance enables these applications to run on Azure App Service while preserving compatibility and reducing operational overhead.

Key benefits include:

  • Built-in App Service capabilities such as autoscale, resiliency, zone redundancy, and Azure service integration.
  • Administrative control through Azure Bastion-enabled RDP access, custom scripts, registry adapters, storage mounts, and identity management.
  • Support for complex workloads, including classic .NET Framework applications, without code changes.
  • Enterprise-ready capabilities, including a 99.95% SLA, Premium v4 performance, Azure Policy integration, Microsoft Defender for Cloud support, and deployment through Bicep, Terraform, and ARM templates.

Get started by assessing eligible workloads with Azure Migrate and deploying through the Azure portal, Azure CLI, or infrastructure-as-code tools.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Ipv6 support in Azure Firewall
items.description:
Azure Firewall now supports IPv6 in public preview, enabling customers to configure Azure Firewall and Firewall Policy in dual-stack mode for both IPv4 and IPv6 traffic. This preview allows native IPv6 network-rule filtering and DNS Proxy support, helping organizations secure cloud, hybrid, and internal IPv6 traffic as they modernize toward dual-stack architectures. 

Learn more.
